story_description: Users designing hooks in the Blaze Hooks Builder need to export their configurations to the correct provider-specific config paths so that the target CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or Codex CLI) can load and execute the hooks during agentic sessions.
task_description: Implement session-aware hook context by passing the active session's provider to the HookRunner, enabling hooks to execute with knowledge of which CLI engine is currently active and allowing provider-specific hook behavior without requiring hooks to detect the engine themselves.
atom_description: A Swift implementation that connects SessionStore session lifecycle events to HookRunner provider context, creating a HookProvider from the session's engineType when a session starts and setting it as the active provider on the HookRunner instance, enabling all subsequent hook executions to access provider-specific context for conditional logic and provider-aware behaviors.
problem_statement: Hooks executing during agentic sessions have no way to know which CLI engine (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) is currently active. This forces hook authors to implement their own engine detection logic, leading to duplicated detection code across hooks, potential detection failures when CLI output formats change, and inability to leverage the session context that Blaze already maintains. Without session-aware hook context, hooks cannot implement provider-specific behaviors reliably.

api_contracts: HookProvider.init(from engineType: EngineType) -> HookProvider? - factory method for engine-to-provider mapping
HookRunner.setActiveProvider(_ provider: HookProvider?) async - sets current session provider context
HookRunner.clearActiveProvider() async - clears provider context (convenience for setActiveProvider(nil))
HookRunner.getActiveProvider() async -> HookProvider? - retrieves current provider context
HookInput.provider: HookProvider? - optional provider field in hook command stdin JSON
event_contracts: HooksEvent.providerSet(provider: HookProvider, previousProvider: HookProvider?) - emitted when setActiveProvider called with non-nil value
HooksEvent.providerCleared(previousProvider: HookProvider?, reason: ProviderClearReason) - emitted when provider context is cleared
ProviderClearReason enum with cases: sessionEnded, engineDisconnected, manualClear - indicates why provider was cleared
SessionEvent.started should now be followed by HooksEvent.providerSet in event sequence
SessionEvent.ended should now be preceded by HooksEvent.providerCleared in event sequence

edge_cases: Session starts with unknown EngineType not in HookProvider mapping - set provider to nil, log warning, hooks execute without provider context
setActiveProvider called while hooks are mid-execution - actor isolation ensures current executions complete with old provider, new executions use new provider
Multiple rapid session switches - each setActiveProvider call overwrites previous, no queue or debounce needed
HookRunner.setActiveProvider called before any hooks registered - provider stored correctly, available when hooks register later
Session ends but endSession not called due to crash - provider remains set until next startSession overwrites or app restart clears
Hook accesses provider field but it is nil - hook should handle nil gracefully as optional value
EngineType enum gains new case in future - init(from:) should return nil for unknown cases with logged warning
Concurrent getActiveProvider calls - actor returns same value to all callers safely
App backgrounded with active session - provider context persists in memory, available on foreground
failure_modes: EngineType to HookProvider mapping has bug returning wrong provider - hooks execute with incorrect provider context, fix requires code update
SessionStore fails to call setActiveProvider on startSession - hooks execute without provider context (degraded but functional)
SessionStore fails to call clearActiveProvider on endSession - stale provider context persists to next session (wrong context)
HookInput JSON encoding fails to include provider field - hooks receive input without provider (degraded but functional)
Hook command fails to parse provider field from JSON - hook continues without provider context (hook author bug, not Blaze bug)
Actor deadlock between SessionStore and HookRunner - should not occur with proper async/await usage, no shared locks
Memory leak if provider enum has associated values that retain references - HookProvider is simple enum with no associated values
rollback_plan: If session-aware hook context causes issues: 1) Remove setActiveProvider/clearActiveProvider calls from SessionStore to disable feature, 2) HookRunner continues to work with nil activeProvider, 3) Hooks receive HookInput without provider field (backward compatible), 4) Revert HookInput struct changes if JSON parsing issues occur, 5) Remove telemetry events if they cause noise. The feature is additive and all code paths handle nil provider gracefully.

risks: EngineType enum changes without updating HookProvider.init(from:) causing mapping failures for new engine types
Race condition between session end and hook execution could pass stale provider context
HookInput JSON schema change could break existing hook parsers expecting old format
Actor reentrancy could cause unexpected provider state if setActiveProvider is called during hook execution
mitigations: Add compile-time exhaustive switch in init(from:) that fails to build when EngineType gains cases
Actor isolation guarantees atomic provider updates - execution uses provider at call time
HookInput.provider is optional with null default - existing parsers ignore unknown fields
Swift actors are reentrant-safe by design - setActiveProvider is simple property set with no async calls
risk_register.blast_radius: Minimal blast radius - affects only provider context field in HookInput. If mapping fails, hooks execute with nil provider (degraded but functional). No impact on session management, UI, or hook execution logic.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If session-aware hook context causes issues: 1) Comment out setActiveProvider/clearActiveProvider calls in SessionStore to disable feature, 2) HookRunner continues with nil activeProvider, 3) HookInput serializes without provider field or with null, 4) Hooks that check provider handle nil case gracefully. Feature is fully additive.
